metadata.note: The Ann Arbor Railroad (1895-1950 passenger) and its predecessors: Toledo - Ann Arbor - Durand - Owosso - Alma - Cadillac - Frankfort/Elberta, with the alignment changes of 1896 (Ann Arbor cutoff, replacing the route via Leland) and 1897 (Ithaca - Alma direct, replacing the route via St. Louis). Features are split by operator era (Toledo and Ann Arbor 1880; Toledo, Ann Arbor and Grand Trunk 1881-84; Toledo, Ann Arbor and North Michigan 1885-95; Frankfort and Southeastern 1889-91; Ann Arbor 1895-1950) and by drawable span; DT&I (1905-10) and Wabash (1925-63) stock control are NOT splits - the trains stayed Ann Arbor trains. Also the AA-owned Manistique and Lake Superior in the Upper Peninsula and its predecessors (each its own company and colour), and the Steam Railroading Institute excursions on the ex-AA line. The Lake Michigan car ferries are ships and are not drawn. Research report: research/branches/ann_arbor_railroad.txt.

segments.note: Southern end of the Toledo - Frankfort main line, via Manhattan Junction, Alexis, Temperance, Lulu, Dundee and Milan. University of Michigan football specials ran to Ann Arbor (years not found). headway_min is an ESTIMATE from train counts, not a timetable reading: 1898 two trains each way south of Mt Pleasant, 1900 three each way Toledo - Ann Arbor (incl. a local) and a Toledo - Cadillac train, 1941-42 one train each way daily except Sunday (51/52).
